# pi-web v0.1.0-beta.1

This beta completes the live frontend cutover. Every live browser route now serves either the React desktop product or the separate React mobile product. Svelte remains only in the self-contained, read-only conversation export.

## Highlights

- Independent desktop and mobile React products with automatic device selection and the `pi-web-surface=desktop|mobile|auto` override.
- Typed shared HTTP, SSE, host, pairing, and session-bootstrap contracts.
- Public-device pairing, paired-device management, and peer navigation across independent pi-web installations.
- Self-contained static conversation snapshots suitable for secret GitHub Gists.
- T3 Code-derived desktop interactions with the upstream revision and MIT license recorded in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

## Security and installation

- The installer no longer generates or prints `PI_WEB_TOKEN`.
- Existing tokens in `~/.config/pi-web/env` are preserved. A token is written only when the operator explicitly passes `PI_WEB_TOKEN` to the installer.
- Token query parameters are rejected. Browser authentication uses form submission followed by a host-only cookie; programmatic clients can use the authorization headers.
- In-place updates preserve the running binary's directory, including unprivileged `~/.local/bin/pi-web` installations.
- Linux auto-start remains a systemd user service and reads `~/.config/pi-web/env`; no system-wide unit is required.

## Production artifacts

The release embeds only:

- React desktop (`web/dist-desktop`)
- React mobile (`web/dist-mobile`)
- static conversation export (`web/dist-export/export.js`)

The former live-Svelte build, rollback cookie, and `/static/assets/*` namespace are removed. Live-Svelte-only panels and routes are not part of this beta.

## Release assets

Prebuilt binaries are published for Linux, macOS, and Windows on both amd64 and arm64:

- `pi-web-linux-amd64`
- `pi-web-linux-arm64`
- `pi-web-darwin-amd64`
- `pi-web-darwin-arm64`
- `pi-web-windows-amd64.exe`
- `pi-web-windows-arm64.exe`

## Upgrade notes

Use the normal package update or rerun `install.sh`. The installer leaves optional token configuration unchanged and does not modify externally managed tunnels. Existing session files and SQLite data require no migration.
